meaning: “I have a diver down; keep well clear at slow speed.”
name: Alfa
usage: Displayed by vessels conducting diving operations when divers are in the water nearby.
individual: When flown alone, it warns other vessels to keep a safe distance and proceed slowly.
example: A dive boat hoists Alfa while divers are working below the surface; nearby boats reduce speed and stay clear.

meaning: “I am taking in, discharging, or carrying dangerous goods.”
name: Bravo
usage: Used when a vessel is handling or transporting hazardous materials.
individual: Warns surrounding vessels that dangerous cargo is involved and additional caution may be required.
example: A tanker handling hazardous cargo displays Bravo while loading operations are in progress.

name: Charlie
usage: Used as a visual affirmative response to another signal or question.
individual: Confirms that the previous message or question should be understood positively.
example: One vessel asks for confirmation; Charlie is hoisted to communicate “Yes.”

meaning: “Keep clear of me; I am maneuvering with difficulty.”
name: Delta
usage: Used when a vessel has limited freedom to maneuver and needs surrounding traffic to stay clear.
individual: Gives other vessels an immediate warning not to approach closely.
example: A vessel performing a difficult maneuver in confined waters displays Delta.

meaning: “I am altering my course to starboard.”
name: Echo
usage: Indicates an intentional course change toward the vessel’s right-hand side.
individual: Communicates a starboard alteration visually to nearby vessels.
example: Before changing direction to starboard, a vessel displays Echo.

name: Foxtrot
usage: Used when a vessel has a problem that prevents normal operation and needs communication with another vessel.
individual: Indicates disabled status and requests contact.
example: A vessel suffering mechanical failure raises Foxtrot to attract the attention of nearby traffic.

name: Golf
usage: Used when a vessel requests pilot assistance. Fishing vessels operating near fishing grounds may use it to indicate that they are hauling nets.
individual: Its primary meaning is a request for a pilot.
example: A ship approaching an unfamiliar port displays Golf while waiting for a pilot.

name: Hotel
usage: Displayed after a maritime pilot has boarded the vessel.
individual: Informs nearby traffic and port services that a pilot is currently aboard.
example: A cargo vessel entering port displays Hotel once the local pilot takes control.

meaning: “I am altering my course to port.”
name: India
usage: Indicates an intentional course alteration toward the vessel’s left-hand side.
individual: Communicates a port alteration to surrounding traffic.
example: A vessel preparing to turn to port displays India.

meaning: “I am on fire and have dangerous cargo on board; keep well clear of me,” or “I am leaking dangerous cargo.”
name: Juliett
usage: Used for a serious hazardous-material emergency involving fire or leakage.
individual: Warns other vessels to keep a significant distance from the affected ship.
example: A vessel carrying hazardous material develops a fire and displays Juliett to warn nearby traffic.

name: Kilo
usage: Used to attract another vessel’s attention and request communication.
individual: Functions as a direct visual request to establish contact.
example: A nearby vessel displays Kilo before beginning an exchange of signals.

name: Lima
usage: Used when another vessel needs to stop immediately.
individual: Gives a direct instruction rather than simply reporting the signaling vessel’s status.
example: A vessel displays Lima to instruct another approaching vessel to stop.

meaning: “My vessel is stopped and making no way through the water.”
name: Mike
usage: Indicates that the vessel is stationary rather than moving through the water.
individual: Reports the vessel’s current movement status.
example: A stopped vessel displays Mike so nearby traffic understands that it is not making way.

name: November
usage: Used as a negative response to a visual or coded question.
individual: Indicates that the preceding message should be understood negatively.
example: A vessel answers a visual question with November to communicate “No.”

name: Oscar
usage: Hoisted immediately when someone falls into the water so nearby vessels can assist with lookout and recovery.
individual: Oscar alone carries the complete man-overboard warning.
combination: SO — “You should stop your vessel instantly.” IMO
example: A crew member falls overboard; Oscar is raised while the vessel begins its recovery maneuver.

meaning: In harbour: “All persons should report on board as the vessel is about to proceed to sea.”
name: Papa
usage: Traditionally known as the “Blue Peter,” it is associated with a vessel preparing to depart. Fishing vessels may have an additional at-sea meaning concerning obstructed nets.
individual: In port it tells required personnel to return aboard before departure.
example: A vessel preparing to leave harbour raises Papa while completing departure preparations.

meaning: “My vessel is healthy and I request free pratique.”
name: Quebec
usage: Traditionally used when requesting health clearance to enter a port.
individual: States that the vessel considers itself free from quarantinable disease and requests permission to proceed under health regulations.
example: An arriving vessel displays Quebec while requesting health clearance.

meaning: No standard standalone single-flag meaning in the current International Code of Signals reference set.
name: Romeo
usage: Primarily used as part of multi-flag code groups rather than as an independent message.
individual: The UI should make it clear that Romeo differs from most alphabet flags because users should not interpret it as a complete standalone sentence.
example: Romeo appears together with other code flags as part of a coded message. TideLab

name: Sierra
usage: Indicates that the vessel’s propulsion is currently operating astern.
individual: Communicates the vessel’s propulsion action to surrounding traffic.
example: A ship maneuvering away from a berth displays Sierra while using astern propulsion.

meaning: “Keep clear of me; I am engaged in pair trawling.”
name: Tango
usage: Used by fishing vessels participating in pair-trawling operations.
individual: Warns other vessels that fishing gear and a second vessel may restrict safe passage nearby.
example: A pair of fishing vessels displays Tango while towing a net between them.

name: Uniform
usage: Used to warn another vessel that its current movement or course is leading toward danger.
individual: Addresses the receiving vessel directly and warns it to reassess the situation.
example: A vessel observes another craft approaching a hazard and raises Uniform as a warning.

name: Victor
usage: Used when assistance is required but the signal itself does not specify the exact type of help needed.
individual: Communicates a direct request for assistance.
example: A disabled vessel displays Victor to request help from nearby vessels.

name: Whiskey
usage: Used when a person aboard needs medical help.
individual: Makes a specific request for medical rather than general assistance.
example: A crew member suffers a serious injury and the vessel raises Whiskey.

meaning: “Stop carrying out your intentions and watch for my signals.”
name: X-Ray
usage: Used to tell another vessel not to continue with its intended action and to wait for further signaling.
individual: Combines an instruction to stop the planned action with a request to remain alert for additional signals.
example: A vessel observes an unsafe maneuver developing and displays X-Ray.

name: Yankee
usage: Used when an anchored vessel is being moved because its anchor is no longer holding securely.
individual: Warns nearby vessels that the ship may move unexpectedly.
example: Strong wind causes an anchored vessel to drift, so Yankee is displayed.

name: Zulu
usage: Used when a vessel requests tug assistance. Fishing vessels operating near fishing grounds can use it with the meaning “I am shooting nets.”
individual: Its general maritime meaning is a request for tug assistance.
example: A large vessel requiring assistance with maneuvering near port raises Zulu.

name: Nadazero
usage: Used as the number zero inside numerical signal groups, positions, measurements, times, bearings, distances, or coded messages.
individual: When displayed as a numeral pennant, it represents the digit 0 rather than a complete standalone instruction.
example: Used as part of a multi-digit value such as 120, where the final pennant represents zero.

name: Unaone
usage: Used wherever the digit one is required in a numerical maritime signal.
individual: Represents the numeric value 1 and is normally interpreted together with the surrounding signal group.
example: A sequence of numeral pennants can use 1 as part of a time, distance, bearing, or position value.

name: Bissotwo
usage: Represents the digit two in numerical groups and coded maritime communication.
individual: Does not carry a separate warning or instruction when used alone; its primary purpose is numerical transmission.
example: The numeral 2 may appear in a signal specifying a quantity, coordinate, or course.

name: Terrathree
usage: Used for transmitting the digit three in numeric information.
individual: Represents 3 within a larger message rather than a complete sentence or command.
example: Used in a three-digit bearing such as 135°.

name: Kartefour
usage: Used in numerical groups for positions, times, measurements, quantities, and other encoded information.
individual: Represents the numeric value 4.
example: It can appear in a time group such as 14:00 or as part of a coordinate.

name: Pantafive
usage: Represents five when transmitting numerical information visually or by Morse.
individual: Its meaning is purely numerical unless used as part of a defined multi-signal code group.
example: A vessel can use the numeral 5 within a reported distance or position.

name: Soxsix
usage: Used to communicate the digit six clearly in numerical maritime messages.
individual: Represents 6 and normally requires surrounding context to understand what the number describes.
example: It may appear in a coordinate, quantity, time, or course value. GovInfo

name: Setteseven
usage: Represents the digit seven in visual and coded numerical communication.
individual: Has no independent operational instruction; it provides a numerical value.
example: Used as part of a value such as 270° or another numerical signal group.

name: Oktoeight
usage: Used for transmitting the digit eight in coded numbers, coordinates, distances, and other numerical data.
individual: Represents the number 8.
example: It can form part of a latitude, longitude, bearing, quantity, or time.

name: Novenine
usage: Represents the digit nine in numerical signal groups.
individual: Used primarily as part of a longer numerical value rather than as an independent message.
example: The pennant can be combined with other numerals to communicate a value such as 090°, 19, or 29.
